info.bio:
Precursores del Emo de la segunda generación (véase antes Embrace, Rites of Spring, Fugazi...) formados en 1992 en  Seattle, Washington , por Dan Hoerner y Nate Mendel (compañeros de piso), William Goldsmith (invitado tras verle actuar Dan y Nate) y Jeremy Enigk, amigo de William desde el instituto.

En 1994 graban su primer disco; "Diary" (Sub-Pop), donde destacan los temas "Seven" e "In Circles" que seguramente sean unas de las composiciones mas influyentes para muchos.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Band Internal Drama
podcast.body: The band was known for significant internal drama, described as a "real-life soap opera." Members frequently quit and returned, with some even finding religion and quitting again. "Plus, this band was a real-life soap opera drama. Members quits, they were turned, they found religion and quit again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Half 90s Emo Band
podcast.body: Sunny Day Real Estate is mentioned as a key emo band from the first half of the 1990s, contributing to the genre's development before its mainstream breakthrough. "In the first half of the 90's, we had Sunday Day real estate and job breaker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members Joined Foo Fighters
podcast.body: Following internal turmoil and departures, the entire rhythm section of Sunny Day Real Estate decided to work with Dave Grohl and subsequently became one half of the Foo Fighters. "And others, including the entire rhythm section, decided that they'd rather work for Dave Grohl and became one half of the food fighters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Seattle Emo Sound
podcast.body: Emerging from Seattle, Sunny Day Real Estate had little in common with the city's prominent grunge bands like Pearl Jam, Nirvana, Soundgarden, or Alice in Chains. They distinguished themselves with a slower, more melodic style, softly sung or crooned vocals (rather than screaming), and occasionally poppy elements. "Sunny day real estate had nothing in common with groups like Pearl Jam or Nirvana or Sound Guard and Aralus and Chains. They played slower than most other emo bands. Their songs were more melodic. And vocals tend to be softly sung or even crooned rather than screamed or shouted. In fact, some of the stuff that they did was downright poppy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
